subject: overnight dogfood loop

decision_impact: Every cycle must research and persist before acting; elapsed time cannot be filled with arbitrary features.

subject: project importance
claim: The user's latest explicit order is God of Sessions first and project-factory second; cam-bow is a low-priority side project; the vibejason.com payment-review task is complete.

subject: Claude billing semantics

decision_impact: Grok Build cannot be treated as an isolated coding-only allowance; competing Grok activity can change the available opportunity.

subject: Codex
claim: Codex provides parallel agents, Automations, memory, proactive work suggestions, long-running work, and mobile steering.
decision_impact: God of Sessions cannot differentiate on generic scheduling, memory, parallel execution, or remote steering alone.

subject: Claude

decision_impact: God of Sessions must explain when and why a cross-provider plan beats a native Claude Routine.

subject: Cursor
claim: Cursor has an Agents Window and scheduled or event-triggered Automations with memory, multi-repo and no-repo operation, and computer-use support.
decision_impact: Cross-provider portfolio judgment, not another automation builder, is the defensible product test.

subject: Grok Build
claim: Grok Build provides an all-session Agent Dashboard, long-running /goal, saved resumable workflows with large agent fan-out, and an open-source harness.
decision_impact: Session overview and long-running orchestration are native capabilities; God of Sessions must compare route suitability rather than claim them as unique.

subject: Hermes upstream

decision_impact: Current Hermes comparisons must include these upstream capabilities while route execution must stay bounded to the installed version.

subject: Hermes installed version
claim: This Mac has Hermes Agent v0.18.2 with one carried local commit, behind upstream v0.19.0.
decision_impact: Do not recommend or claim v0.19-only execution behavior on the installed Hermes route.

subject: OpenClaw upstream
claim: The latest verified OpenClaw release is v2026.7.1 with durable goals and task flows, Workboard proof artifacts, usage views, and current desktop/mobile control surfaces.
decision_impact: Current market comparison must include this broader control-plane surface.

subject: OpenClaw installed version
claim: This Mac has OpenClaw 2026.4.26, materially behind upstream 2026.7.1.
decision_impact: Treat installed OpenClaw route capabilities as stale and do not infer current upstream task/approval behavior locally.

subject: installed agent versions
claim: Observed local versions are Codex CLI 0.145.0-alpha.30, Claude Code 2.1.220, Grok Build 0.2.112, Hermes 0.18.2, and OpenClaw 2026.4.26.
decision_impact: Version-stamp each route decision and test capability rather than assuming current documentation matches the installed binary.

subject: Agent Sessions
claim: Agent Sessions is an MIT local-only native macOS app that searches and resumes histories across Codex, Claude, Cursor, Hermes, OpenClaw and other tools and attributes quota burn to individual sessions.
decision_impact: A unified session browser and quota meter are commodity boundaries, not the launch wedge.

subject: OpenUsage
claim: OpenUsage locally monitors quotas, spend, limits, model use, and burn across dozens of coding tools and API platforms.
decision_impact: God of Sessions should consume or validate capacity truth, not compete as a deeper usage analytics dashboard.

subject: Conductor
claim: Conductor coordinates Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode sessions in isolated workspaces from one Mac app.
decision_impact: Multi-harness execution in one GUI is already available and is not sufficient differentiation.

subject: long-running work
claim: Anthropic's long-running harness experiments found that compaction alone was insufficient; initializer state, an explicit feature list, incremental work, durable progress artifacts, clean checkpoints, and end-to-end testing reduced common failures.
decision_impact: An overnight goal contract should bound incremental work and require outcome evidence rather than merely allocating hours.

subject: dogfood evaluation
claim: Agent evaluation should distinguish the transcript or trajectory from the final environment outcome and combine deterministic, model-based, and human grading where appropriate.
decision_impact: Morrow's prose cannot be treated as success when the approval payload or workspace state disagrees.

subject: objective and causal memory
claim: AMA-Bench reports that similarity-based memory systems underperform when they omit objective and causal information; its proposed system combines a causality graph with tool-augmented retrieval.
decision_impact: Store why a project was promoted, demoted, completed, or superseded rather than only retrieving similar transcript text.

subject: environment experience
claim: LongMemEval-V2 evaluates static recall, dynamic state tracking, workflow knowledge, environment gotchas, and premise awareness; file-backed agent retrieval outperformed the strongest RAG baseline but cost more latency.
decision_impact: Use compact decision state plus searchable evidence and explicit gotchas; do not dump all transcripts into every prompt.

subject: differentiation
claim: Provider-native dashboards plus Agent Sessions, OpenUsage, and Conductor make unified session viewing, basic input-needed sorting, quota display, and multi-harness launching insufficient standalone differentiation.
decision_impact: Evaluate God of Sessions on cross-provider project judgment, authority consistency, and morning evidence.

subject: God of Sessions thesis
claim: The strongest current wedge is deciding which project should run on which actually available route, using explicit user goals, fresh source-specific capacity, conflicts, risk, wake time, and exact evidence—then keeping chat, approval, receipt, and morning review consistent.
decision_impact: Dogfood scenarios and product changes should attempt to falsify this thesis rather than assume it.

subject: no-run recommendation
claim: In the current eight-hour expert scenario, the deterministic overnight tool returned zero candidates and Morrow preserved that empty portfolio instead of inventing a runnable project.
decision_impact: Preserve no-run as a first-class successful recommendation behavior.

subject: capacity freshness disclosure
claim: Morrow labeled Codex fresh, Grok stale after an approximately eleven-hour-old successful value and current billing failure, and Claude stale after an approximately forty-hour-old value and timeout.
decision_impact: Keep observation time, current fetch state, and stale labels visible; do not route on a reassuring old percentage.

subject: route comparison evidence
claim: The chat compact overnight payload omits route_inventory and dispatch_preflights; when asked to compare routes, Morrow misused search_sessions with a concatenated capability query and then produced partially unsupported route explanations.
decision_impact: Expose structured route and preflight evidence and prohibit session search from being presented as a capability probe.

subject: exact plan handoff
claim: Clicking Review in Overnight after an eight-hour chat plan opened an idle Overnight screen with no plan and a default seven-hour input. Chat persists only a suggested view, not the exact plan or duration.
decision_impact: Treat chat-to-approval continuity as a P0 before adding more orchestration features.

subject: context synchronization

decision_impact: Cycle 02 may proceed because current evidence was structured before acting.

subject: canonical approval scope
claim: OpenClaw prepares and stores one canonical systemRunPlan for node-host execution, reuses that stored plan after approval, and rejects later changes to command, raw command, working directory, agent, or session metadata as an approval mismatch.
decision_impact: Bind God of Sessions approval to an immutable typed plan fingerprint and fail closed on any scope drift.

subject: Codex app-server approval lifecycle
claim: Codex app-server scopes approval requests by thread, turn, item, environment, and request identity; resolved requests are cleared on lifecycle transitions and item/completed is the authoritative execution result.
decision_impact: Approval UI state must be correlated to the exact active plan and terminal result, not a global or previously visible selection.

subject: Grok permission and plan modes
claim: Grok Build keeps plan review independent from Auto and Always-approve modes, separates sandbox constraints from permission decisions, and gives deny rules precedence over allow rules.
decision_impact: A permissive provider mode must not bypass God of Sessions' frozen-plan review boundary.

subject: elicitation correlation
claim: The MCP elicitation specification requires clients to correlate completion with the initiating elicitation ID and ignore unknown or already-completed IDs.
decision_impact: Expired or superseded approval identities must never revive authority when a late event arrives.

subject: durable task handles
claim: MCP Tasks model long-running work as durable receiver-created state machines that can be polled after reconnect, expose working/input-required/terminal states, and are durably created before the task response is sent.
decision_impact: Overnight dispatch needs durable external run identities and reconnectable status, not a blocking tool call or transcript-only promise.

subject: Codex app-server limits
claim: Codex app-server currently exposes primary and secondary rate-limit windows, reset timestamps, optional monthly limits and spend-control state, earned reset credits with expiry, sparse updates, and account usage summaries.
decision_impact: Replace fixed five-hour/weekly assumptions with typed capacity-pool observations and preserve reset credits as separate idempotent resources.

subject: Grok paid usage
claim: Grok paid products now consume one shared weekly pool across Chat, Build, Imagine, Voice, and other surfaces; workload compute cost varies and extra credits are distinct from the included pool.
decision_impact: A Grok Build recommendation must account for opportunity cost against the user's other Grok products and cannot treat its percentage as an isolated coding quota.

subject: Claude subscription limits
claim: Claude Code distinguishes rolling session, weekly, model-specific, and temporary server limits and directs users to /usage for current reset and allowance information.
decision_impact: Claude capacity must retain limit type, model scope, freshness, and reset time instead of one normalized remaining percentage.

subject: Claude subscription authentication
claim: Anthropic states that third-party developers may not offer Claude.ai login or route requests through Free, Pro, or Max credentials on users' behalf; developers should use API keys or supported cloud providers.
decision_impact: Do not productize copied Claude consumer OAuth; use supported API billing or dispatch through the user's native installed Claude Code surface under its own contract.

subject: routine completion semantics
claim: Claude Routines documents that a green run only means the session started and exited without an infrastructure error; users must inspect the transcript because blocked tools and task-level failures can still mean the requested work did not succeed.
decision_impact: Morning review must independently judge workspace and test outcomes rather than map provider completion directly to success.

subject: session management commodity boundary
claim: Claude Agent View, Cursor durable side chats and local transcript search, GitHub Agent HQ and Chronicle, Grok Workflows, OpenClaw gateway dispatch, Conductor, and OpenUsage collectively make session lists, search, memory, scheduling, model routing, and quota dashboards table stakes by July 2026.
decision_impact: Focus launch and dogfood on cross-project portfolio judgment, exact authority, and verified morning outcomes rather than another session browser.

subject: independent outcome grading
claim: Current agent-evaluation guidance treats the final environment state as distinct from the transcript and recommends a separate evaluator with a concrete rubric; Anthropic's Outcomes pattern uses a stateless grader that independently inspects evidence and returns revision gaps.
decision_impact: Convert every dogfood defect into a regression and grade real UI, persisted state, and workspace outcome independently from Morrow's prose.

subject: structured context synthesis
claim: OpenAI and Anthropic now describe background memory synthesis that merges duplicates, replaces stale or contradicted entries, surfaces new insights, preserves reviewability, and keeps the input store unchanged.
decision_impact: Maintain an append-only evidence ledger plus a replaceable reviewed current-context synthesis rather than injecting raw session history or silently editing provenance.

subject: approval scope drift
claim: Code review of the exact chat handoff found that the handoff's 15-minute expiry could be replaced by a 30-minute registry window, the registry was not bound to the visible plan fingerprint, duration changes invalidated only frontend state, and reopened stored plans were not revalidated before approval registration.
decision_impact: Cycle 02 must implement typed plan fingerprints, absolute expiry, explicit invalidation, stored-plan revalidation, and stale-plan rejection before further feature work.

subject: context synchronization
claim: The third synchronization window ran for ten active minutes and two seconds from 11:46:49 to 11:56:51 PDT and pressure-tested the portfolio-judgment thesis against current protocols, provider documentation, product contracts, open-source competitors, and agent research before deriving the next dogfood trial.
sources: web research trace in current Codex task
decision_impact: Cycle 03 may use the revised competitive boundary because the evidence was structured before the next trial.

subject: MCP Tasks lifecycle
claim: MCP Tasks requires a task to be durably created before its handle is returned, asks clients to persist task IDs for reconnect, separates working and input_required from completed/failed/cancelled terminal states, makes terminal states immutable, and treats cancellation as cooperative.
decision_impact: Use durable provider run handles and honest lifecycle states, but do not confuse runtime completion with portfolio value or task success.

subject: Codex app-server
claim: Codex app-server is a version-specific rich-client protocol with persisted thread/turn/item primitives, streamed item lifecycle, scoped approvals, terminal completion events, and rate-limit and usage state; generated schemas are explicitly tied to the installed Codex version.
decision_impact: Version-stamp and generate the installed schema instead of maintaining a timeless hand-written Codex contract; use terminal item evidence as runtime truth.

subject: OpenClaw approval enforcement
claim: OpenClaw documents separate gateway and host execution policy layers, applies the stricter effective result, denies when required approval UI is unavailable under fail-closed fallback, and binds final forwarding to the stored canonical systemRunPlan rather than mutable command fields.
decision_impact: God of Sessions must enforce exact authority at the final host side-effect boundary as well as at UI preparation; unavailable approval surfaces must never widen permission.

subject: Claude scheduled execution
claim: Claude Code now documents session-scoped recurring prompts through scheduled tasks and persistent cloud Routines that can run without approval prompts and use selected connectors; Routine green status reports infrastructure completion rather than task-level success.
decision_impact: Scheduling itself is no longer a wedge. God of Sessions must justify what should be scheduled, bound its authority, and independently verify the outcome.

subject: GitHub agent session management
claim: GitHub's agents panel monitors sessions across repositories, exposes logs, token usage and duration, traces commits to validation logs, supports steer/stop/archive for Copilot, and answers natural-language questions across synced session history; steering is not available for third-party coding agents.
decision_impact: Session query, monitoring, and history-grounded chat are table stakes; cross-provider control and pre-delegation portfolio judgment remain separate tests.

subject: Hermes current product surface
claim: Hermes release documentation now describes evidence-based completion contracts, /journey and a desktop memory graph, first-class coding projects backed by project→repo→lane, background subagent fan-out, and selectable Mixture-of-Agents models.
decision_impact: Projects, personality-backed memory, model ensembles, background delegation, and 'done proven' are no longer sufficient God of Sessions differentiation.

subject: Hermes Kanban
claim: Hermes Kanban is a shared SQLite task board whose model tools and CLI use the same database; tasks and handoffs survive restarts, support human comments, crash reclaim, dependencies, idempotency keys, runtime bounds, persistent audit rows, and per-project boards.
decision_impact: A durable multi-agent queue and audit trail are execution substrate features, not the portfolio-judgment wedge.

subject: Conductor
claim: Conductor runs Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode in isolated workspaces and orchestrates sessions, terminals, diffs, checks, and pull requests. Its API cookbook begins after the user supplies a coding task and explicit model, then asks a manager to select a repository and supervise execution.
decision_impact: Do not compete on workspace orchestration alone; test whether Morrow can choose the valuable task and project before handing work to a Conductor-like layer.

subject: Agent Sessions
claim: The current Agent Sessions repository presents a local-first macOS app for browsing, searching, analyzing, resuming, and tracking limits across Codex, Claude Code, Cursor Agent, Hermes, OpenClaw, and other coding-agent histories.
decision_impact: Existing-session import, search, resume, and quota attribution are an established category; God of Sessions must add a higher-level decision.

subject: Claudexor execution substrate
claim: Claudexor is an MIT local-first control plane for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, and raw APIs with multiple subscription profiles, live quota and opt-in rotation, shared threads with bounded continuation packets, content-hashed plans, deterministic gates, durable artifacts, best-of-N, council planning, delegated sub-runs, and bounded repair loops.
decision_impact: Treat Claudexor as a serious execution/control-plane counterexample and possible MIT substrate subject to a compatibility, license, and runtime audit; do not reimplement it blindly.

subject: Claudexor product boundary
claim: Claudexor's constitution explicitly defines it as a coding-harness control plane rather than a digital entity with personality, memory identity, or an autonomous runtime doctrine; its public flows operate on selected projects and user-supplied ask/plan/agent objectives.
decision_impact: A user-specific judgment/personality layer over existing fragmented histories remains architecturally distinct, but must be proven rather than assumed.

subject: quota-aware overnight scheduling
claim: A current MIT community tool, ai-schedule, runs user-authored Claude Code prompts in a chosen folder when live five-hour or weekly quota conditions match. A user response asks for clean git or worktree state, runtime/token caps, allowed paths, ambiguity stops, and rollback before trusting it overnight.
decision_impact: Quota-conditioned scheduling is emerging as a commodity, while unattended safety and choosing the useful task remain user pain signals.

subject: AgentPulse recommendation and watcher
claim: AgentPulse documents a durable AI watcher queue, conversational command surface, cross-project inbox, human-gated continuation, MCP fleet control, and an experimental API-only launch recommendation for agent/model/host based on prior completions at the same cwd; its existing launch validator remains authoritative.
decision_impact: AgentPulse is the closest inspected recommendation counterexample, but its published recommendation scope is route advice within one cwd rather than autonomous cross-project ROI selection.

subject: Longhouse
claim: Longhouse publicly describes automatic cross-provider local session ingestion into one searchable timeline plus managed launch, send, interrupt, steering, resume, phone/browser control, and a local SQLite runtime host for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other agents.
decision_impact: Automatic existing-session discovery and remote control are no longer unique; portfolio choice must sit above session operations.

subject: Happier
claim: Happier publicly documents a unified encrypted interface across many coding agents with takeover of existing Codex/Claude/OpenCode sessions, persistence, cross-device handoff, subagents, a voice assistant with session context, an inbox, approval-gated actions, queued messages, and steering.
decision_impact: A characterful chat or voice operator that sees and controls every session is already competitive territory; Morrow must contribute cross-project judgment, not only conversational control.

subject: Code-by-wire
claim: Code-by-wire publicly presents a local-first MIT control room for Claude Code and Codex with automatic session discovery, search/resume/fork/observe, reconstructed transcripts, embedded terminals, live context/token/cost/git/task telemetry, history, and rate-limit reset visibility.
decision_impact: A polished session rail, telemetry, history, and limit display are commodity surfaces; the God of Sessions graph should visualize decisions and eliminations instead.

subject: Kansei
claim: Kansei publicly describes local coordination of Claude, Codex, local models, and terminals across projects, with self-forming teams, dependencies, peer review, delegated questions, stalled-run recovery, mobile control, subscriptions or keys, and longer unattended runs; its flow starts from a mission supplied by the operator.
decision_impact: Kansei is a strong cross-project execution counterexample. God of Sessions must choose the mission from evidence before a Kansei-like layer coordinates it.

subject: Latch
claim: Latch publicly describes local multi-harness governance with per-session worktree isolation, one policy across agents, network and secret controls, replay, checkpoints, budgets, consistent MCP and skill injection, and Ed25519-signed receipts containing a policy hash and audit-log Merkle root.
decision_impact: Governance, isolation, audit replay, and cryptographic receipts are not standalone differentiation; God of Sessions should define which work deserves that governed execution.

subject: Operator
claim: The inspected Operator project is a kanban-shaped multi-agent orchestration application that detects Claude, Codex, and Gemini CLIs and launches tickets through configured delegator tuples of harness, model, and optional model server.
decision_impact: Kanban ticket launch and model-server routing are execution mechanics after work is defined; they do not by themselves solve portfolio selection.

subject: OpenAI Symphony
claim: OpenAI reports that engineers comfortably manage only about three to five simultaneous Codex sessions before context switching hurts productivity, and Symphony shifts the control plane from sessions and PRs to deliverables represented as issue-tracker tasks.
decision_impact: God of Sessions should reason over project goals, tasks, and deliverables rather than make the session object its primary unit of value.

subject: human planning and domain expertise
claim: Anthropic's privacy-preserving analysis of roughly 400,000 Claude Code sessions reports that people make most planning decisions while Claude makes most execution decisions, and that task-specific domain expertise is associated with more verified success and better recovery from errors.
decision_impact: The unresolved high-value layer is grounded planning about what to do and what counts as done; Morrow must preserve and apply the user's domain judgments.

subject: long-running coding work
claim: Anthropic's long-running-agent experiments found that incremental one-feature-at-a-time work, descriptive git checkpoints, durable progress files, recoverable state, and explicit end-to-end testing mitigate scope drift, repeated rediscovery, and false completion.
decision_impact: An eight-hour allocation is not a useful goal by itself; every selected task needs bounded scope, recoverability, and a concrete morning oracle.

subject: cross-session proactivity
claim: π-Bench evaluates hidden user intents, inter-task dependencies, and cross-session continuity separately from task completion; its reported frontier-model experiments find proactive assistance remains difficult and that prior interaction helps later intent resolution.
decision_impact: Dogfood must score attention saved and latent-priority recovery separately from whether a generated task can be executed.

subject: bounded competitive finding
claim: In the public documents inspected for Claudexor, AgentPulse, Longhouse, Happier, Code-by-wire, Kansei, Latch, Conductor, Operator, Agent Sessions, and ai-schedule, no product explicitly claimed to read fragmented existing cross-provider histories and autonomously select the highest-ROI project and task for an overnight portfolio with contrastive elimination and a no-run option.
decision_impact: Treat portfolio judgment as a falsifiable opening, not an established monopoly; keep searching and test against the closest overlaps.

subject: revised God of Sessions thesis
claim: The narrowest defensible current hypothesis is portfolio judgment before delegation: recover real user priorities from fragmented histories, compare project value with fresh route capacity and safety, explain why every alternative lost, preserve no-run, freeze one exact authority, and independently prove the morning outcome.
decision_impact: The next real-app trial must compare at least three real projects without the user supplying the winner, task, or provider; failure to add a decision above AgentPulse, Claudexor, and Kansei falsifies the thesis.

subject: portfolio visualization
claim: Because session timelines and cockpits are already common, the product's differentiating visualization should be tested as a decision graph from fragmented evidence through candidate ranking, constraints and eliminations, selected or no-run outcome, exact authority, and morning proof.
decision_impact: Do not add another generic session graph before the portfolio decision itself passes dogfood.
recheck_after: after portfolio-judgment trial and user testing

claim: Current Codex app-server documentation exposes structured account rate-limit and usage surfaces with primary and secondary windows plus optional monthly limit, spend control, reset-credit, and activity information; sparse updates require merging or refetching.

subject: Claude subscription authentication
claim: Anthropic's current Claude Code legal documentation says developers building products should use API keys or supported cloud providers and may not offer Claude.ai login or route requests through Free, Pro, or Max credentials on behalf of users.
decision_impact: A productized Claude-subscription advisor route requires policy review and must not copy consumer OAuth; the UI must distinguish a supported local harness from a generally supported third-party subscription provider.

subject: deterministic recommendation scoring

decision_impact: The current planner can rank noisy recent or completed work above older explicit priorities; its semantic value judgment should be replaced rather than expanded with more hand-tuned weights.

subject: Claude individual plan multipliers
claim: Anthropic lists Pro at $20/month, Max 5x at $100/month with 5x Pro capacity per session, and Max 20x at $200/month with 20x Pro capacity per session. Five percent of a Max 20x five-hour session allowance is therefore approximately one full Pro session allowance.
decision_impact: Compare a verified Claude five-hour session window using base-Pro equivalents while keeping provider-native exhaustion and reset rules authoritative.

subject: Claude weekly and model-specific normalization
claim: Anthropic documents five-hour session, weekly all-model, and model-specific limits separately. The inspected primary plan table guarantees 5x or 20x Pro capacity per session but does not prove that every weekly or model-specific denominator scales by the same multiplier.
decision_impact: Label non-session Claude base-plan conversion as an estimate or leave it unavailable; never present it as an exact weekly allowance.

subject: Codex individual plan multipliers and variable task cost
claim: OpenAI lists Plus at $20, Pro $100 at 5x Plus, and Pro $200 at 20x Plus. Codex draws from a shared agentic pool and actual consumption varies by model, tokens, cache, complexity, and execution surface.
decision_impact: Use a plan-equivalent allowance as a routing estimate, never a guaranteed task count, and keep credits or reset rights separate.

subject: exact local subscription tier evidence

subject: cross-provider recommendation capacity score

decision_impact: This is the cycle 05 release-blocking defect. Add plan-aware capacity evidence and a regression where 5% Max 20x outranks 30% of a base plan when all other facts are equal.

subject: durable completion loops in Codex Claude and Grok
claim: Current Codex app-server exposes stable thread/goal/set, get, clear, and updated methods; Claude Code supports noninteractive /goal loops with an independent evaluator; and Grok Build supports /goal with persistent status, verification, pause, resume, and bounded headless execution. These provider-native goal loops are the appropriate execution primitive for an overnight completion promise.
sources: local read-only source inspection of /private/tmp/morrow-research-openai-codex and /private/tmp/morrow-research-grok-build
decision_impact: Dispatch Codex through thread/goal/set and send slash-leading /goal objectives to Claude and Grok; do not call an ordinary one-turn prompt a goal run.
recheck_after: any supported provider CLI or protocol upgrade

subject: overnight completion contract versus current workers
claim: The local Codex, Claude, and Grok workers currently submit an ordinary structured prompt. Codex waits for the first turn/completed, while Claude and Grok merely bound one noninteractive invocation with max-turns. Grok's ledger nevertheless reports goal_mode true. A successful process can therefore look like a goal run without provider-native completion evidence.
decision_impact: This is cycle 06's release-blocking defect. Replace ordinary prompts with native goals and require a terminal goal status before morning success.

subject: long-running goal authority and untrusted history
claim: Long-running agent loops magnify prompt-injection, stale-permission, sandbox-escape, and lucky-pass risks. Session histories must remain untrusted evidence rather than executable instructions, provider settings must be established before continuation, and morning success must include outcome verification rather than process exit alone.
decision_impact: Keep the frozen authority envelope, deny external actions, cap runtime, and record requested and effective execution facts separately from provider success.
recheck_after: any authority, prompt, sandbox, or verification change

subject: Mac sleep prevention during overnight work
claim: A possible next defect was host sleep readiness, but the current workers already wrap detached provider processes with /usr/bin/caffeinate -i and the product already exposes host readiness. This does not survive lid close, manual sleep, shutdown, or low-power interruption, but duplicating idle-sleep prevention would not fix the current vertical slice.
decision_impact: Do not spend cycle 06 on another power widget. Correct the false goal execution and receipt first; durable crash and wake recovery remains a later cycle.

subject: Claude provider-owned terminal Goal evidence
claim: Claude Code 2.1.220 persists /goal evaluator results as transcript attachments. A non-sentinel attachment with type goal_status, met true, and a condition containing the exact run marker is durable provider-owned completion evidence. met false without failed remains nonterminal, while failed true is terminal failure; process exit alone is not Goal completion.
sources: local read-only structural inspection of existing Claude transcript goal_status attachments without exposing transcript content
decision_impact: Persist Claude goal_status in the local receipt, parse only bounded exact-marker transcript events, fail closed on missing or active status, and require marker plus met true before presenting a morning success.
recheck_after: Claude Code transcript schema or /goal evaluator change
